sources: Regional food traditions of Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan

summer.name: Grishma (summer)
summer.principle: Classical texts advise sweet, light, cooling and well-hydrated foods, as the heat depletes the body.
summer.favour: Ragi ambli or porridge, jowar, buttermilk, gourds, cucumber
summer.avoid: Very spicy, oily or heavy fried food

monsoon.name: Varsha (monsoon)
monsoon.principle: Digestion is weak in the rains, so the texts advise warm, freshly cooked, light food with mild spices like ginger and cumin.
monsoon.favour: Warm jowar and bajra rotis, moong dal, drumstick, ivy gourd
monsoon.avoid: Raw salads, stale or cold food

winter.name: Hemanta-Shishira (winter)
winter.principle: Strong digestion in the cold months suits nourishing, warming and unctuous food, such as grains with a little ghee or sesame.
winter.favour: Bajra, ragi, methi, palak, carrot, horse gram, ghee
winter.avoid: Cold drinks and excessively light, dry meals

ragi.lore: Ragi is a traditional Kudhanya (coarse grain), the staple of Karnataka mudde, and is cooling and filling, with exceptional calcium.

jowar.lore: Jowar is the daily bhakri grain of Maharashtra and Karnataka, light on the stomach and suited to most seasons.

bajra.lore: Bajra is the winter grain of Gujarat and Rajasthan, valued as warming and strengthening, and rich in iron.

moong.lore: Moong is regarded in Ayurveda as one of the lightest, easiest-to-digest pulses.

toor.lore: Toor dal is the everyday dal of western and southern India and balances the grain's amino acids.

chana.lore: Chana dal adds fibre and sustained energy, common in Maharashtrian and Gujarati cooking.

horse.lore: Horse gram (kulthi, hurali) is a traditional warming pulse of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, high in calcium and iron.

principles: Millet plus pulse is the traditional khichdi logic: grains are low in lysine and pulses supply it, so together they form a better protein.
Fermenting or soaking (ragi dosa, ambli, idli) is traditionally used to make grains easier to digest and minerals easier to absorb.
Add a sour or vitamin C source like lemon or raw mango to improve absorption of iron from millets and greens.
Eat local and seasonal: the vegetables of the season are the ones the body needs in that season.
